summary: Section 4 test-only repair of documented step M4-S05 for F-59 (reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M5.md run 4): every method of CaseMilestoneServiceTest now runs its action and assertions inside System.runAs of a user minted by TestUserFactory.createUser holding Case_Agent_Core + Case_Tier1 (the exact member list of PSG_Tier1_Prod, artefacts/M2-S02/permissionsetgroups) on Profile 'Acme Support Tier 1' -- the closest persona in this build to 'a Tier 1 agent working a case'. TestDataFactory.cls was replaced with a verbatim copy of the corrected template (commit 5edcb3281, the null-lookup guard). caseInsideProcess gained a User agent parameter and wraps only its Case insert in System.runAs(agent); the Account/Entitlement inserts in entitlementFor stay ambient because Case_Agent_Core grants only Read on both. No assertion, message string, or Test.startTest/stopTest boundary was added, removed or changed. CaseMilestoneService.cls and CaseMilestoneTrigger.trigger are unchanged byte for byte. This step has no package.xml (the Apex exception, standards/build-orchestration.md section 5); M5-S05's build-level manifest needs a fifth ApexClass member (TestUserFactory) that this step records as an obligation rather than writing itself.
confidence_rationale: Both declared and requested checkers exit 0 (check_entitlement_apex_hooks.py: 5 files, 0 ERROR/0 WARN under --strict; check_test_class_standards.py: user-mode-test-without-runas 0, score 100). check-outputs is ok on all 8 declared paths, and both copied template classes diff empty against their canonical sources. Confidence is capped at MEDIUM, not HIGH, because: (1) no offline Apex compiler exists (agents/apex-builder/GATES.md Gate D) so this repair is confirmed only by the next dry run (run 5), not executed by this agent; (2) the specific field(s) that failed FLS in run 4's probe were never isolated by name -- no e.getDmlFieldNames(0) probe was captured, so the fix follows the established Gotcha 13/14 pattern rather than a field-level diagnosis of this build's own failure; and (3) whether Case_Agent_Core + Case_Tier1 actually grant enough FLS for every field caseOverrides sets (Origin, Priority, EntitlementId) and for CaseMilestone.CompletionDate is a claim this design-only build cannot verify without an org.

findings.title: F-59 addressed: every test method now runs inside System.runAs of a Tier 1 agent
findings.detail: The org rejected all three org-executed methods at their Case insert because no runAs block existed for a permissioned user and the shipped TestDataFactory predated the null-lookup guard. mintAgent() mints a user via TestUserFactory.createUser(AGENT_PROFILE, AGENT_PERMISSION_SETS) inside a mixed-DML fence (System.runAs(new User(Id = UserInfo.getUserId()))), and every one of the four @IsTest methods now wraps its Case DML, its CaseMilestoneService call, and its assertions in System.runAs(agent).

findings.title: Permission-set choice: Case_Agent_Core + Case_Tier1, matching PSG_Tier1_Prod
findings.detail: Case_Tier1 is a delta permission set with no object permissions of its own (record-type visibility and Case.Severity__c edit only) -- it composes with Case_Agent_Core for base Case CRU. Together they are exactly the member list PSG_Tier1_Prod declares for 'the 12 Tier 1 agents' (artefacts/M2-S02/permissionsetgroups/PSG_Tier1_Prod.permissionsetgroup-meta.xml), paired with Profile 'Acme Support Tier 1' whose own description says all its object/field/tab access comes from that group. Case_Tier2 was rejected as an identical-but-differently-named footprint (artefacts/M2-S02/deploy-order.md: Tier1/Tier2 'carry identical grants'); Case_Billing was rejected because it withholds the Support record type and this test is not record-type-scoped; Case_Intake_Integration was rejected as the intake-side persona, not the agent-working-a-case persona this trigger serves.
findings.recommendation: None -- recorded as the grounding for a choice the task required, not a defect.

findings.title: Account and Entitlement fixture creation deliberately stays outside System.runAs(agent)
findings.detail: Case_Agent_Core grants Read only, never Create, on Account and Entitlement. caseInsideProcess (via entitlementFor) creates both; a real Tier 1 agent could not, so this repair does not wrap that half of the fixture in the agent's context. Only the Case insert the permission set actually grants Create on, and everything downstream of it, runs as the agent. caseInsideProcess gained a User agent parameter for this reason.

evidence.note: objectPermissions: Account allowCreate=false, Entitlement allowCreate=false, Case allowCreate=true

findings.recommendation: If a future persona needs to prove it can also create the Entitlement fixture, that is a separate test against a different permission-set combination, not a change to this one.

findings.title: A checker-parsing hazard in check_test_class_standards.py was found and worked around
findings.detail: strip_literals in the checker blanks single-quoted spans but does not exclude comments (its own docstring says so). Three pre-existing possessive apostrophes in this class's comments (unrelated to this repair) shifted the checker's left-to-right quote pairing enough to make every System.runAs(agent) call in the class invisible to has_permissioned_runas on the first two verification attempts, even after the fix was correctly written in code. Rephrasing those three comments (and avoiding new apostrophes in comments this repair added) resolved it; no Apex behaviour changed.
findings.recommendation: Flagged for build-doc-keeper to carry forward as a skill-tooling defect: strip_literals should exclude // and /* */ spans before pairing quotes, or the rule should operate on method bodies only.

process_observations.observation: Both the declared checker and the requested check_test_class_standards.py run clean under --strict, and check-outputs confirms all 8 declared paths are still present -- the repair is auditable as a small, targeted diff rather than a rewrite.

The tier2-webhook build's earlier repair of the identical defect (S2-F-11/S2-F-12, artefacts/M1-S03/deploy-order.md section 0b/0c) gave this repair an accepted shape to follow rather than inventing one -- the mixed-DML fence and the System.runAs placement are copied from that precedent, not designed fresh.

Four separate dry runs of this build (M4 and the first three M5 runs) carried runTestsEnabled: false and were treated as sufficient evidence for the M4 gate. A validation that compiles but never executes a test is not evidence the test passes, and this is the second build in this session (after tier2-webhook) where that gap produced a HIGH finding only once --test-level was finally passed.

A stdlib text-scanning checker that does not exclude comments from its quote-pairing logic is a landmine for any future author whose prose comments near permissioned code contain an odd number of apostrophes -- it fails silently (reports the old, wrong finding) rather than erroring out on unparseable input.

Whether Case_Agent_Core + Case_Tier1 actually grant sufficient FLS for CaseMilestone.CompletionDate and for the Case fields caseOverrides sets (Origin, Priority, EntitlementId) is unverified in a design-only build. The permission sets grant no explicit CaseMilestone object permissions at all in this build, consistent with CaseMilestone access typically following the parent Case's Edit permission rather than carrying its own CRUD grant, but that inference is not confirmed against an org.
M5-S05's package.xml needs a fifth ApexClass member (TestUserFactory) before the next manifest-mode dry run will see a complete deploy.
